Following the Springer correspondence for a unipotent element of Jordan type \lambda in \mathrm{GL}_n, the top cohomology of the Springer fibre carries the irreducible S_n-module V_\lambda (Tonny A. Because the normalized Markov-trace weighted sum \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\,\chi^\lambda(\beta)\,\Delta_\lambda is intensive, no per-partition scalar weight \Delta_\lambda can generate the super-pairwise extensive nuclear binding energy documented in Term 6 binding density. Any genuine closure of the many-body binding magnitude must therefore arise from an irreducibly super-pairwise (\ge 3-body) extensive mechanism rather than a re-weighting of \Delta_\lambda.

Phenomenological depth-two recurrences are not derivations. Discrete depth-two q-difference recurrences w_{n+1} = a_0 w_n + r_{\mathrm{res}} w_{n-1} on the [n]_q!-normalized carrier (distinct up to scalar gauge from the resurgent Stokes carrier of Stavros Garoufalidis, Jie Gu, and Marcos Mariño [garoufalidis-gu-marino2021]) reproduce multi-body binding hierarchies only when seeded with calibrated phenomenological constants (a_0 = 1/2, r_{\mathrm{res}} \approx 2.596, and empirical isospin shifts). rem:tjon-universality-external:
Remark The external three-body/four-body correlation, and why it does not license the simplex baseline. The many-body magnitude leg of \Delta_\lambda (Per-partition \Delta_\lambda value versus open super-pairwise many-body binding magnitude) is scored against an external observable—the empirical correlation between three-body and four-body binding energies, known in nuclear physics as the Tjon line. Separating what the effective-field-theory literature establishes from the inclusion--exclusion simplex expansion prevents an analogy from being misread as a derived premise.

The external results

Two results are used.

No four-body parameter at leading order. Working in an effective theory of short-range interactions whose two-body scattering length a is large compared with the natural low-energy length scale \ell of the interaction (|a| \gg \ell), Lucas Platter, Hans-Werner Hammer, and Ulf-G. Meißner find that an \mathrm{SU}(4)-symmetric one-parameter three-nucleon interaction suffices to renormalise the four-nucleon system at leading order in \ell/|a|; the empirical triton--\alpha correlation then follows by varying that single three-body parameter [platter2005tjon]. With the binding energies B({}^2\mathrm{H}) = 2.22\,\mathrm{MeV} and B({}^3\mathrm{H}) = 8.48\,\mathrm{MeV} as inputs they obtain B(\alpha) \approx 29.5\,\mathrm{MeV} for the \alpha-particle, against a Coulomb-corrected experimental 29.0 \pm 0.1\,\mathrm{MeV}.

A dimensionless four-to-three ratio. Solving the four-boson Yakubovsky equations with no four-body parameter, Hans-Werner Hammer and Lucas Platter report that away from threshold the four-body ground state and the deepest three-body state are related by a factor of 5 [hammer2007fourbody]. The correlation is approximately linear away from threshold for either sign of a, with positive curvature for a > 0 and negative curvature for a < 0; the nonlinearity is confined to the threshold region.

Limits of the external results

Each of the following is a separate statement that the results above do not license:

  1. "No four-body parameter is needed" is not "no four-body force exists." The first is a statement about leading-order renormalisation; the second is a statement about physical interactions. The four-nucleon force is small, not absent: Eric D. Jurgenson, Petr Navrátil, and Richard J. Furnstahl evaluate the similarity-renormalisation-group-induced four-body contribution at {}^4\mathrm{He} as a net effect of order tens of keV, with the long-range \mathrm{N}^3\mathrm{LO} estimate of order a few hundred keV [jurgenson2009srg].

  2. The leading-order claim is contested in general. Yamashita et al. find a strong sensitivity of the deepest four-body energy to a four-body subtraction constant, concluding that a four-body parameter should generally enter at leading order. As noted in [hammer2007fourbody], both analyses agree on the nuclear case because short-range repulsion suppresses four-particle contact configurations, while general universality rests on the inherited renormalisation-group power counting.

  3. The zero-range limit is not the nuclear regime. The universal ratio 5 is a zero-range result, whereas experimental nuclear binding from AME2020 [ame2020] gives B({}^4\mathrm{He})/B({}^3\mathrm{H}) \approx 3.42 after Coulomb correction; [platter2005tjon] attributes the shift of its leading-order Tjon line to neglected finite-range effects.

Inequivalence with the simplex condition

Expanding the many-body binding moment in an inclusion--exclusion simplex basis,

  M(A) \;=\; \sum_k \mu_k \binom{A}{k},

translates the naive ansatz \mu_4 = 0 into M(4) = 4M(3) - 6M(2). That algebraic condition is provably inequivalent to leading-order three-body renormalisability. On the \mu_4 = 0 baseline, M(4) < 4\,M(3) holds strictly for every \mu_2 > 0 and arbitrary \mu_3 (with deficit -6\mu_2), placing the universal zero-range ratio M(4)/M(3) = 5 outside the reachable cone. Conversely, substituting M(4) = 5\,M(3) forces

  \mu_4 \;=\; 9\mu_2 + \mu_3,

so \mu_4 is largest precisely in a four-boson calculation carrying zero four-body interaction input. Because three moments fitted to three anchors (A = 2, 3, 4) determine an exact algebraic identity

  \mu_4 \;:=\; M(4) - 4M(3) + 6M(2),

\mu_4 measures only the departure of M(4) from the two-point binomial extrapolation, not an irreducible physical four-body potential. The external Tjon-line literature therefore motivates tracking departures from two-point extrapolation, without deriving the simplex baseline or licensing a four-body force interpretation of \mu_4.

prf:borromean-h4-categorical-derivation:
Proof Proof of borromean h4 categorical derivation. The proof proceeds in two structural steps.

Step 1 — Schur–Weyl + R-matrix derivation of \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}).

The q-Schur duality for \mathrm{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) and \mathrm{H}_3(q) gives a (\mathrm{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), \mathrm{H}_3(q))-bimodule decomposition

  V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3}
  \;\cong\;
  V_{3/2} \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  V_{1/2} \otimes S^{(2,1)}

(dimensions: 4 \otimes 1 \;\oplus\; 2 \otimes 2 \;=\; 4 + 4 = 8). Tracing on the V^{\otimes 3} side via the standard ordinary trace (matching the \mathrm{H}_n(q)-side classical-dim convention) gives:

  \mathrm{tr}_{V^{\otimes 3}}(F(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}))
  \;=\;
  \dim(V_{3/2}) \cdot \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;+\;
  \dim(V_{1/2}) \cdot \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  4 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}),

where F is the q-Schur duality functor sending the braid generators \sigma_i to the braided R-matrices \check{R}_{i, i+1} acting on V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3}, and \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1 since \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} has writhe 0 and projects to the identity in S_3.

The braided R-matrix is

  \check{R}(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
    0 & q - q^{-1} & 1 & 0 \\
    0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\
    0 & 0 & 0 & q
  \end{pmatrix}

in the basis \{|\!\!\uparrow\uparrow\rangle, |\!\!\uparrow\downarrow\rangle, |\!\!\downarrow\uparrow\rangle, |\!\!\downarrow\downarrow\rangle\}, satisfying the Hecke relation (\check{R} - q)(\check{R} + q^{-1}) = 0. Its inverse is

  \check{R}^{-1} \;=\; \check{R} - (q - q^{-1}) I,

derived from the Hecke quadratic relation \check{R}^2 = (q - q^{-1})\check{R} + I (this is not \check{R}(q \to q^{-1}), which is the universal R-matrix not the braided form). Setting \sigma_1 = \check{R} \otimes I_2, \sigma_2 = I_2 \otimes \check{R} as 8 \times 8 matrices on V^{\otimes 3}, direct computation of \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2)^3 gives:

  \mathrm{tr}_{V^{\otimes 3}}(F(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}))
  \;=\;
  8 - 6h^4 - 2h^6
  \quad\text{(exact, verified to 50 digits at the aether \(q_0 \approx 1.10998\)).}

Subtracting 4 \cdot 1 and dividing by \dim(V_{1/2}) = 2 yields:

  \chi^{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  2 - 3h^4 - h^6,

i.e. the h^4 coefficient is -3. (This polynomial form is also derivable directly from the closed form of Borromean Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2 + 4) via the substitution u = q^2 + q^{-2} = h^2 + 2; the R-matrix derivation provides the categorical confirmation.)

Step 2 — Markov normalisation y_{(2,1)}(q=1) = 1/[2]_q^2|_{q=1} = 1/4.

The Frobenius expansion of the Markov trace on \mathrm{H}_3(q):

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} y_\lambda(q) \cdot \chi^\lambda(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  y_{(3)}(q) + y_{(2,1)}(q)\!\cdot\!(2 - 3h^4 - h^6) + y_{(1^3)}(q),

using \chi^{(3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = \chi^{(1^3)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = 1. Regrouping:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{\bigl[y_{(3)} + 2\, y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}\bigr]}_{= \,\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}_3) \,=\, 1 \text{ (Markov norm.)}}
  \;+\;
  y_{(2,1)}(q) \cdot (-3h^4 - h^6),

since the Markov normalisation gives \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \cdot d_\lambda = \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}_3) = 1 for the identity braid. The h^4 coefficient is therefore

  \bigl[h^4\text{-coeff of }\mathrm{tr}_M\bigr] \;=\; -3 \cdot y_{(2,1)}(q=1).

From the closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6) / (h^2 + 4) the h^4 coefficient is -3/4 (exact symbolic series division). Solving:

  -3 \cdot y_{(2,1)}(q=1) \;=\; -\tfrac{3}{4}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  y_{(2,1)}(q=1) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{4} \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q^2|_{q=1}}.

The factor [2]_q^{c-1} is the standard Markov-trace normalisation for closure of an n-strand braid into a c-component link: for the Borromean rings (c = 3), [2]_q^2 = h^2 + 4 is exactly the denominator in the closed form \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}) = (\cdots)/(h^2 + 4).

The identity y_{(2,1)}(q) = 1/[2]_q^2 in fact holds exactly for all q, not only at q = 1: the full closed-form weight vector on \mathrm{H}_3(q) is y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3, y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2, y_{(1^3)} = 0 (identically — the Temperley–Lieb quotient kills the 3-row partition), evaluating at q = 1 to the non-uniform vector (\tfrac12, \tfrac14, 0). See Closed-form Jones/Temperley–Lieb weights on H_3(q) (Borromean Jones polynomial) for the derivation and for why a bar-involution uniformity argument fails (the Jones-normalised trace is chiral — not invariant under the sign-twist automorphism \sigma \mapsto -q\,\sigma^{-1}).

Combining Steps 1 and 2.

  \bigl[h^4\text{-coeff of }\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})\bigr]
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{(-3)}_{\text{Step 1: R-matrix on }V_{1/2}^{\otimes 3}}
  \;\cdot\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{4}}_{\text{Step 2: Markov norm. for }c = 3}
  \;=\;
  -\tfrac{3}{4}. \qquad \square

Connection to the wider framework

The two ingredients each acquired a categorical home elsewhere in the framework after the initial derivation:

  • Step 1 (the polynomial form χ^{(2,1)}(β_Bor) = 2 − 3h⁴ − h⁶) shares its Wedderburn partition-indexed framework with the q-heat-kernel Peter–Weyl decomposition and the Habiro residue-sum equivalence.   -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2}\, \zeta(3).

Step 2 (take real part). \zeta(3) \in \mathbb{R} is real. \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_N^k) = \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) by definition.

Therefore

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2}\, \zeta(3).

Step 3 (parity reduction for odd N). By \mathrm{Cl}_3 parity:

  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi (N - k)/N)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi - 2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N).

For odd N, the indices k = 1, \ldots, N - 1 pair as (k, N - k), giving (N - 1)/2 pairs. Therefore

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  2 \sum_{k = 1}^{(N - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N),

and dividing by 2:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{(N - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{2 N^2}\, \zeta(3).

For even N, the middle term k = N/2 gives \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi) = \sum_{j \geq 1} \cos(j\pi)/j^3 = \sum_{j \geq 1} (-1)^j/j^3 = -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) (alternating Dirichlet series for \zeta(3)), and the other (N - 2)/2 pairs contribute symmetrically. The closed form then takes the form recorded above (N = 2 in the table below verifies -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) directly). \square

N = 2 special case: \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi)

At N = 2, the sum has a single term \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi):

  \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi) \;=\; -\frac{3}{4} \zeta(3).

This is the classical evaluation \mathrm{Li}_3(-1) = -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) (real, no imaginary part — consistent with Trilogarithm imaginary part at \zeta_n: closed form (n - 1)(n - 2)\pi^3 / (3 n^3) for every root of unity giving \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_2) = 0).

Asymptotic behaviour

As N \to \infty:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;\to\;
  -\zeta(3),

approaching from below. The fractional remainder \frac{1}{N^2}\zeta(3) captures how close to "saturating" \zeta(3) the orbit sum is. This reflects the Riemann-sum interpretation:

  \int_0^{2\pi} \mathrm{Cl}_3(\theta) \,d\theta \;=\; 0,

so as the discretisation tightens, the sum tends to the integral modulo boundary corrections, which include \zeta(3) from the k = 0 contribution \mathrm{Cl}_3(0) = \zeta(3).

rem:cyclotomic-depth3-dimension-synthesi:
Remark Upper-bound sketch for cyclotomic depth3 dimension synthesis. Sketch.

Step 1 (count starting generators). The cyclotomic Galois orbit of \zeta_K consists of \varphi(K) = K - 1 primitive Kth roots of unity. Grouped by complex-conjugate pairs (since \overline{\zeta_K^j} = \zeta_K^{K-j}), the orbit yields (K - 1)/2 pairs.

For each pair \{\zeta_K^j, \zeta_K^{K-j}\}, the corresponding \mathrm{Li}_3 values give:

  • One real part \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi j/K) = \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j) (bar-fixed in \mathcal{P}_3^+).
  • One imaginary part S_3(2\pi j/K) = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j) (bar-twisted in \mathcal{P}_3^-, related to its conjugate by sign).

Total: (K - 1)/2 real parts + (K - 1)/2 imaginary parts = K - 1 candidate generators.

Step 2 (eliminate imaginary parts via Theorem A). By Trilogarithm imaginary part at \zeta_n: closed form (n - 1)(n - 2)\pi^3 / (3 n^3) for every root of unity:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j)
  \;=\;
  \frac{(jK - 1)(jK - 2)\,\pi^3}{3\,(jK)^3}
  \quad \text{(?)}

Wait — the formula applies at \zeta_n with n = K/\gcd(j, K). For prime K and 1 \leq j \leq K - 1, \gcd(j, K) = 1, so \zeta_K^j is itself a primitive Kth root. Apply Theorem A at n = K:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{sign}(\ldots) \cdot
  \frac{(K - 1)(K - 2)\,\pi^3}{3\,K^3} \cdot (\text{sign from } j).

More precisely: \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j) = S_3(2\pi j/K) where S_3 is bounded in magnitude by the closed-form expression (K - 1)(K - 2)\pi^3/(3K^3) at the principal angle. By the multi-angle Tate-rational structure (Step 1 above), every imaginary part is a \mathbb{Q}-linear combination of \pi^3 — i.e., lies in the 1-dim Tate-line \pi^3 \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathcal{P}_3.

Under the Beilinson regulator quotient \mathcal{P}_3 \to \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathrm{Tate}, all (K - 1)/2 imaginary parts collapse to zero. They contribute zero dimensions to \mathcal{V}_K.

Step 3 (count residual real-part dimensions). The (K - 1)/2 real parts \{\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi j/K) : 1 \leq j \leq (K - 1)/2\} satisfy:

  • Orbit-sum relation by General orbit-sum identity: \sum_k \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) = -(N^2-1)/N^2 \cdot \zeta(3) at every N \geq 2:

      \sum_{j=1}^{(K - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi j/K)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{K^2 - 1}{2K^2}\,\zeta(3).

    This is one linear relation modulo \mathcal{V}_K — it pulls a 1-dim component into the \zeta(3)-line, which projects to zero in \mathcal{P}_3 / (\mathcal{P}_2 + \mathbb{Q}\zeta(3)).

Therefore the remaining \mathbb{Q}-rank of the real parts modulo \mathcal{V}_K is at most:

  \frac{K - 1}{2} - 1 \;=\; \frac{K - 3}{2}.

Step 4. Combining Steps 2 (imaginary parts contribute 0) and 3 (real parts contribute at most (K - 3)/2):

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_K \;\leq\; \frac{K - 3}{2}.

\square

Lower bound — conditional on Beilinson

Claim. \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_K \geq (K - 3)/2, conditional on Beilinson's conjecture at \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K).

Argument. Borel's theorem: for prime K, \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K) is totally complex with r_2 = (K - 1)/2. For n = 3 (odd):

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K)) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;=\;
  r_2 \;=\; \frac{K - 1}{2}.

This \frac{K - 1}{2}-dim space includes the \zeta(3)-line (rank 1, traces from K_5(\mathbb{Z}) \otimes \mathbb{Q}); modding out gives a Borel-predicted (K - 3)/2-dim "genuinely-new" component.

Beilinson's conjecture at \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K) asserts that the Beilinson regulator image saturates this Borel rank — i.e., the (K - 3)/2 genuinely-new dimensions are all realised in \mathcal{V}_K. Combined with the upper bound:

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_K \;=\; \frac{K - 3}{2}
  \quad \text{(conditional on Beilinson).}

prop:jonquiere-cyclotomic-tate-rationali:
Proposition General Jonquière Tate-rationality: wrong-parity part of \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) has closed form -(2\pi i)^n / n! \cdot B_n(1/K) at every depth. For every depth n \geq 2, the wrong-parity part of \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) obeys a uniform Bernoulli-polynomial closed form:

  \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) - (-1)^{n - 1}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^{-1})
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{n!} \cdot B_n\!\left(\tfrac{1}{K}\right).

The wrong-parity part—the imaginary part for odd n and real part for even n—evaluates as Tate-rational at every depth. It contributes zero to the Beilinson regulator image. The genuinely new period content isolates precisely to the right-parity part. This dictates why the depth-2 imaginary \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2 and the depth-3 real \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3 carry the true periods.
prf:jonquiere-cyclotomic-tate-rationalit:
Proof Proof of jonquiere cyclotomic tate rationality. Step 1 (Jonquière inversion formula, Lewin 1991 §7). For z \notin (0, 1) and n \geq 1:

  \mathrm{Li}_n(z) \;=\; (-1)^{n - 1}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(z^{-1})
  \;-\; \frac{(2\pi i)^n}{n!} B_n\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{\log(-z)}{2\pi i}\right),

where the principal branch of \log is taken.

Step 2 (specialise at z = \zeta_K = e^{2\pi i/K}, K \geq 2). Here -\zeta_K = e^{i (2\pi/K + \pi)}. For K \geq 2, the angle 2\pi/K + \pi exceeds \pi, so the principal log subtracts 2\pi:

  \log(-\zeta_K) \;=\; i\pi (2 - K)/K.

Compute the Bernoulli argument:

  \frac{1}{2} + \frac{\log(-\zeta_K)}{2\pi i}
  \;=\; \frac{1}{2} + \frac{2 - K}{2K}
  \;=\; \frac{K + (2 - K)}{2K}
  \;=\; \frac{1}{K}.

The Bernoulli polynomial evaluates at 1/K — a particularly clean specialisation. Substituting into Step 1:

  \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) - (-1)^{n - 1}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^{-1})
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{n!}\,B_n(1/K).

Step 3 (extract real / imaginary part on unit circle). Since \zeta_K^{-1} = \overline{\zeta_K}, \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^{-1}) = \overline{\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K)}.

  • n odd: (-1)^{n - 1} = 1. LHS = \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) - \overline{\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K)} = 2 i\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K).
  • n even: (-1)^{n - 1} = -1. LHS = \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) + \overline{\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K)} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K).

Therefore:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{2 i \cdot n!}\,B_n(1/K), \qquad n \text{ odd},
  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{2 \cdot n!}\,B_n(1/K), \qquad n \text{ even}.

Both expressions are rational multiples of \pi^n — Tate-rational. \square

Verification at low depths

n = 2 (even, Re part): B_2(x) = x^2 - x + 1/6.

  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(\zeta_K)
  \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi i)^2}{4}\,B_2(1/K)
  \;=\; \pi^2 \left(\tfrac{1}{K^2} - \tfrac{1}{K} + \tfrac{1}{6}\right).

At K = 2: \pi^2(1/4 - 1/2 + 1/6) = -\pi^2/12 (= \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(-1)). (yes)

n = 3 (odd, Im part): B_3(x) = x^3 - 3x^2/2 + x/2.

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K)
  \;=\; \frac{(n-1)(n-2)\pi^3}{3 n^3}
  \quad \text{(see Theorem A)}.

This is the special case n = 3 — recovers Trilogarithm imaginary part at \zeta_n: closed form (n - 1)(n - 2)\pi^3 / (3 n^3) for every root of unity.

n = 4 (even, Re part): B_4(x) = x^4 - 2x^3 + x^2 - 1/30.

  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_4(\zeta_K)
  \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi)^4}{2 \cdot 4!}\,B_4(1/K)
  \;=\; -\frac{\pi^4}{3}\,B_4(1/K).

n = 5 (odd, Im part): B_5(x) = x^5 - 5x^4/2 + 5x^3/3 - x/6.

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_5(\zeta_K)
  \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi)^5}{2 \cdot 5!}\,B_5(1/K)
  \;=\; -\frac{2 \pi^5}{15}\,B_5(1/K).

prop:cyclotomic-orbit-sum-all-depths:
Proposition General orbit-sum at every depth: \sum_k \mathrm{Cl}_n(2\pi k/N) = (N^{1-n} - 1)\zeta(n) for n odd, 0 for n even. For all depths n \geq 2, the orbit sum evaluates as:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_n\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi k}{N}\right)
  \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    \bigl(N^{1 - n} - 1\bigr)\, \zeta(n) & \text{\(n\) odd}, \\[4pt]
    0 & \text{\(n\) even}.
  \end{cases}

For odd depths, the sum isolates exactly one dimension of classical \zeta(n) content. For even depths, the antisymmetric values pair-cancel, leaving all (N-1)/2 magnitudes independent. The dimension count strictly bifurcates by parity: (K-3)/2 for odd depths, and (K-1)/2 for even depths.
